summary: Keep the primary records even when related data is absent.
syntax: SELECT ... FROM primary_table LEFT JOIN related_table ON join_condition;
documentation: LEFT JOIN preserves every row from its left input. If no right-side row satisfies the join condition, the right-side columns in that result row are NULL.
inputs: Two inputs and a relationship expressed in ON.
returns: Matched rows plus unmatched left-side rows with NULL right-side values.
caution: A right-table filter in WHERE can remove unmatched rows. Consider whether a condition belongs in ON instead.
scenarios: List all customers, including those without a booking.
Show every product even when it has no sales yet.
Report every staff member, including those without an assignment.
title: Include customers without jobs
problem: Return customers.id AS customer_id and jobs.id AS job_id for every customer, including customers without jobs. Order by customer_id, then job_id ascending.
goal: Use LEFT JOIN or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Keep customers on the left and join jobs using the customer ID.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;
